title: Band-9 Samples: Do you invite your neighbours to your home? [Why/why not?]
passage_html:
This post contains ideas and band-9 sample answers (audio included) for the Cambridge IELTS 14 Academic Speaking Part 1 Question 2 Test 3 question:

“Do you invite your neighbours to your home? [Why/why not?]”

Sample 1: Yes

Yes, I actually do invite my neighbours to my home quite frequently. The primary reason behind this is that I believe in fostering a sense of community and camaraderie amongst those who live in close proximity. By hosting informal gatherings and sharing meals, we are able to develop stronger bonds and create a more harmonious living environment.

Sample 2: Yes

To be honest, I don’t directly invite our neighbours to our home, as I currently live under my parents’ roof and the responsibility of extending such invitations falls on them. My parents generally have a cordial relationship with the people next door, so it’s quite common for them to welcome neighbours over for various gatherings and festivities.

Sample 3: Yes

Indeed, I do welcome my neighbours into my abode, especially when I host social gatherings or casual get-togethers. This practice helps break the ice and encourages a friendly rapport among all of us. I believe that fostering positive relationships with neighbours is essential to create a safe and congenial environment, where everyone feels comfortable to reach out for assistance or simply enjoy each other’s company.

Sample 4: Yes

Absolutely! As someone with an extroverted disposition, I often host gatherings at my residence and extend invitations to my neighbours. I genuinely enjoy engaging in stimulating conversations and sharing experiences with those around me, as it enriches my social life and promotes a sense of togetherness within our neighbourhood.

Sample 5: No

I must admit, I don’t typically invite my neighbours to my home. This is predominantly due to my introverted nature and preference for solitude. While I do acknowledge the importance of maintaining neighbourly relations, I find it more appropriate to engage in small talk or exchange pleasantries in shared spaces, such as the apartment lobby or local park.

Sample 6: No

To be honest, I seldom ask my neighbours over to my residence, as I value my privacy and often prefer tranquil moments. I believe that maintaining a certain level of distance helps preserve healthy boundaries and avoid potential conflicts. However, I do make an effort to engage with them during neighbourhood events or casual encounters, ensuring that our relationship remains cordial and respectful.

Sample 7: No

Regrettably, I don’t often invite my neighbours to my home, mainly due to our conflicting schedules and varying lifestyles. Given the fast-paced nature of modern life, it can be challenging to find a suitable time for everyone to gather and unwind. Nonetheless, I strive to maintain amicable relations by participating in neighbourhood activities or exchanging greetings when our paths cross.

Sample 8: No

To be candid, I rarely invite my neighbours to my compact living quarters. Given the limited space available, hosting gatherings can be quite a challenge. Instead, I opt for alternative ways to bond with my neighbours, such as meeting up at nearby cafes, parks, or joining local clubs. This approach enables us to maintain amicable relationships while acknowledging the spatial constraints of my domicile.

Sample 9: It Depends

I selectively invite my neighbours to my home, depending on the occasion and the level of familiarity we share. I find it essential to strike a balance between being approachable and preserving my personal space. By inviting neighbours on a case-by-case basis, I can establish genuine connections with those who share common values, while still maintaining a sense of autonomy and respecting each other’s boundaries.

Sample 10: It Depends

To be honest, it depends on the specific neighbour and the rapport we share. I am more inclined to invite neighbours who share similar interests or values, as it facilitates engaging conversations and fruitful connections. However, I am cautious about extending invitations to those with whom I have not yet established a rapport, in order to maintain a comfortable and secure home atmosphere.
